node.name: search
node.description: search the web, answer a question with citations, or extract content from known URLs
node.whenToUse: you need information from the live web — current events, documentation, sources, facts beyond your training.

rootEntry.concept: web search for agents — find pages, get grounded answers, extract page content (Exa)
rootEntry.description: search the web, answer a question with citations, or extract content from known URLs
rootEntry.whenToUse: you need information from the live web — current events, documentation, sources, facts beyond your training. Use web for relevant pages with excerpts, answer for one synthesized cited answer, and contents for clean text from URLs you already hold. This reaches public pages read-only, not logged-in pages or service APIs. Needs an Exa API key (EXA_API_KEY or ~/.crouter/exa.key).

node.summary: web search via the Exa API — find pages, answer questions with citations, extract page content
node.model: Three leaves split by what you have and what you want. `web` is the default: a query in, ranked pages out with query-relevant highlight excerpts (or full text with --text) — use it for discovery and research. `answer` collapses a question into one synthesized, source-cited answer — use it when you want the conclusion, not a reading list. `contents` does no searching; it extracts cleaned content from URLs you already hold. Highlights are the default content mode everywhere (token-predictable); full text is opt-in and length-capped. Every leaf needs an Exa API key resolved on this machine from EXA_API_KEY or ~/.crouter/exa.key; a keyless call fails before any request is sent.

children.name: web
children.description: find web pages relevant to a query, with highlight excerpts
children.whenToUse: you need to discover web pages relevant to a query and read query-matched excerpts from them — the default web search. Use this for open-ended research, finding sources, or gathering current information. Reach for `answer` instead when you want one synthesized, cited answer to a specific question rather than a ranked list of pages; reach for `contents` when you already hold the URLs and only need their content.
children.summary: web search via Exa — ranked results with query-relevant highlight excerpts (or full text)

params.name: query
params.constraint: The search query. Natural language; be specific.

params.name: type
params.constraint: Search depth. auto balances relevance and speed; fast/instant trade depth for latency; deep-lite/deep/deep-reasoning run multi-query expansion and rank the combined set for harder synthesis.

params.name: text
params.constraint: Return cleaned full page text (capped at 4000 characters per result) instead of highlight excerpts. Off by default; highlights keep token usage predictable.

params.name: include-domains
params.constraint: Comma-separated domain allowlist — restrict results to these domains.

params.name: exclude-domains
params.constraint: Comma-separated domain blocklist — drop results from these domains.

output.name: results
output.constraint: Ranked best-first, each: title, url, published date and author when present, and either highlight excerpts (default) or capped full text (--text).

output.name: follow_up
output.constraint: Decision road sign: either read selected result URLs through `crtr search contents` after checking its schema, or refine the query.

effects: Sends one search request to the Exa API (network). No local state changes.

children.name: answer
children.description: get one grounded, cited answer to a question
children.whenToUse: you have a specific question and want a single synthesized answer grounded in sources, rather than a ranked list of pages to read yourself. Best for factual lookups and "what/who/when" questions where you want the conclusion plus its citations. Reach for `web` instead when you want to browse and judge the raw results, or when the task is open-ended research rather than one answerable question.
children.summary: grounded answer via Exa — one synthesized natural-language answer plus the sources it cites

params.name: question
params.constraint: The question to answer. Natural language; phrase it as a question.

output.name: answer
output.constraint: The synthesized natural-language answer grounded in the cited sources; empty when Exa returns no answer.

output.name: citations
output.constraint: The sources the answer draws on, each: title and url when Exa supplies them.

output.name: follow_up
output.constraint: Concrete next command — read a citation in full, or fall back to raw results.

effects: Sends one answer request to the Exa API (network). No local state changes.

children.name: contents
children.description: extract clean content from URLs you already have
children.whenToUse: you already hold one or more URLs — from a prior `search web`/`answer`, a database, an RSS feed, or user input — and need their cleaned content or highlights. This does NOT search; it only extracts from the URLs you give it. Reach for `web` when you still need to find the pages, and `answer` when you want a synthesized response rather than raw page content.
children.summary: content extraction via Exa — cleaned highlights or full text for URLs you already have

params.name: urls
params.constraint: One or more URL tokens to extract. Each token may contain URLs separated by commas or whitespace.

params.name: text
params.constraint: Return cleaned full page text (capped at 4000 characters per URL) instead of highlight excerpts. Off by default.

params.name: max-age-hours
params.constraint: Maximum acceptable age of cached content, in hours; content older than this is freshly crawled. 0 forces a fresh crawl every time. Omit to use cache when available and crawl as fallback.

output.name: results
output.constraint: One per successfully extracted URL, each: title, url, published date and author when present, and either highlight excerpts (default) or capped full text (--text).

output.name: failures
output.constraint: URLs Exa could not fetch, each: url and reason. Empty when every URL extracted.

output.name: follow_up
output.constraint: Concrete next command for retrying failures or refreshing stale content.

effects: Sends one contents request to the Exa API (network). No local state changes.
